original_question: Let X be a smooth contractible complex affine algebraic surface of log-general type. Does X contain any once-punctured curve?
target_in_paper: §1.1, p. 14 (M. Zaidenberg): "Does X contain any once-punctured curve? Does it contain only a finite number of such curves?" for a smooth contractible surface X of log-general type.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient class of objects (smooth complex affine algebraic surfaces), the contractibility hypothesis, the log-general-type regime, and the core existence question about once-punctured curves asked in §1.1. Including "affine" is faithful to the paper, since §1.2 immediately notes that every smooth contractible algebraic surface is affine.
missing_details: The official formulation in §1.1 has two parts: after asking whether X contains any once-punctured curve, it also asks whether X contains only finitely many such curves.
To make the question fully stand-alone, "log-general type" should be spelled out as: the logarithmic Kodaira dimension kappa(X) is 2.
To remove ambiguity, "contractible" should refer to the underlying complex-analytic/topological space of X being contractible.
To remove ambiguity, "once-punctured curve" should be defined explicitly as a smooth affine algebraic curve whose smooth projective completion has exactly one point at infinity.
To make "contain" precise, one should say that X contains an algebraic subcurve isomorphic to such a once-punctured curve.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth complex contractible affine algebraic surface with logarithmic Kodaira dimension kappa(X)=2. Does X contain an algebraic curve Gamma that is a smooth once-punctured curve, i.e. a smooth affine curve whose smooth projective completion has exactly one point at infinity? More generally, is the set of such curves in X finite?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Zaidenberg's question in §1.1. On p. 14 the paper says, after reviewing the kappa(X)=1 case and the known absence of simply-connected curves in the log-general-type case: "Does X contain any once-punctured curve? Does it contain only a finite number of such curves?" Your draft reproduces the first half of this official formulation almost verbatim. The nearby context matters: §1.1 contrasts the well-understood kappa(X)=1 situation with the open log-general-type case, and §1.2 explains why affineness can be taken for granted for smooth contractible algebraic surfaces. The paper does mention analogous questions for Q-acyclic surfaces and for embeddings of C* into X, but it does not state these as equivalent reformulations of the contractible case, so they should not replace the original question.
